Beat 6: She constantly risked commercial Hollywood standing to fund daring independent cinema, sleeping in art museum glass boxes.

Beat 7: Ranked by The New York Times among the greatest actors of the century, she proves true art lives in total reinvention.

posts.comment:
**The secret behind her chameleonic reign:**
• Traces her Scottish family lineage back over one thousand years to the Middle Ages.
• Won the Best Supporting Actress Academy Award in 2008 for her chilling corporate turn in Michael Clayton.
• Performed The Maybe, a live endurance art exhibit sleeping inside an open glass container at MoMA.

Beat 1: **He was living in his car and painting houses for food, then revolutionized sci-fi cinema forever as the T-1000.**

Beat 2: Born November 5, 1958, Robert Patrick turns 68 today, born in Marietta, Georgia.

Beat 3: Surviving a near-fatal boating accident on Lake Erie, he drove across America to Hollywood, living out of his beat-up car while broke.

Beat 4: Auditioning for James Cameron, he studied predatory animal movements and mastered sprinting without blinking or breathing through his mouth.

Beat 5: Terminator 2: Judgment Day shattered box office records, establishing his mimetic polyalloy T-1000 as the definitive action villain of the nineties.

Beat 6: The terrifying perfection of the T-1000 threatened to permanently trap him in emotionless villain roles across the industry.

Beat 7: He broke free with gritty, layered dramatic turns in The X-Files, Walk the Line, and Peacemaker, cementing a legendary four-decade career.

Beat 8: **Was the T-1000 the single greatest and most unstoppable sci-fi villain in movie history?**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind the liquid metal machine:**
• Lived out of his car while working as a bartender and house painter before landing his breakout role.
• Trained rigorously with a martial arts coach to sprint at Olympic speeds without visible chest heave or open-mouthed panting.
• Kept catching up to Edward Furlong's dirt bike during filming because he ran too fast.

Was Terminator 2 the greatest action movie ever made?
posts.reel_script: Before terrorizing audiences as the greatest liquid-metal assassin ever created, a struggling Georgia native lived out of his car and painted houses in Los Angeles. Landing the role of a lifetime opposite Arnold Schwarzenegger, he studied sharks and eagles to sprint without panting or blinking. Four decades later, his cold robotic stare still haunts cinema. Was the T-1000 more terrifying than the original Terminator?
posts.reel_caption: Did you know Robert Patrick trained himself to sprint at full speed without breathing through his mouth for Terminator 2? He outran motorcycles on foot. Who was the scariest villain? #RobertPatrick #Terminator2 #T1000
